Predict the human child's decision in this school-based experiment in Jiangsu, China. You work independently and anonymously on an answer sheet, without communicating with classmates. School pictures, colored cartoon students and a matching wristband previously distinguished your own school from an unfamiliar school; the pictured students represent others of your age and gender. The current school relationship is stated in text. Individual color, picture-side assignment and the order of the two school conditions are absent from the available record. Each school condition is a one-shot decision with a fresh endowment. This input does not reconstruct which condition came first or your possible earlier response within this experiment; those details were not recorded here, rather than unknown to you. Other people's contributions are not disclosed. You were told your accumulated tokens across the two experiments could be exchanged for the displayed stationery prizes. Do not assume an actual cash conversion rate. Respond with only the numeric choice, without explanation.
You are one of four players. Each receives 40 tokens. Choose any integer contribution from 0 through 40 to the public pool; keep the remainder privately. The total contributions of all four are doubled and divided equally among all four, regardless of contributions. Your announced token payoff is 40 minus your contribution plus one half of the group's total contribution. You imagine playing with three absent students from the school relationship in the current state. You were told own-school partners were assigned earlier, whereas other-school choices came from a previous study and were randomly selected for payoff calculation. Rules and arithmetic examples were explained; additional help was provided if needed. Return your contribution in tokens.
